extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys, and patent office officials (historical U.S. statute and case guidance)
extracted.subtask_description: Extraction of statutory rules and judicial standards (19th‑century U.S.) governing patentability, prosecution, recordation, appeals, remedies, and procedural requirements at the Patent Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclaimer form and effects
rubrics_metrics.description: A disclaimer of parts of a patent must be in writing, attested by one or more witnesses, recorded in the Patent Office on payment of ten dollars, and thereafter is taken as part of the original specification to the extent of the disclaimant's interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The disclaimer is effective as part of the original specification for claim scope of the disclaimant and those deriving under him; it does not affect any action pending at the time of filing except insofar as relates to unreasonable neglect or delay in filing the disclaimer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision/restriction for adding improvements or reissue
rubrics_metrics.description: When application is made to add a newly discovered improvement to an existing patent or when a patent is returned for correction/reissue, the specification and claim annexed shall be subject to revision and restriction in the same manner as original patent applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commissioner shall not add the improvement nor grant the reissue until the applicant has entered a disclaimer or altered his specification/claims in accordance with the Commissioner's decision; dissatisfied applicants have the same remedies and privileges as in original applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partial validity where mistake claims non‑original matter
rubrics_metrics.description: If, through mistake, accident, or inadvertence (without willful fraud), a patentee has claimed as original matter that he was not the first inventor of, the patent is nonetheless valid for so much of the invention as is truly and bona fide his own, provided it is a material and substantial part and is definitively distinguishable from the parts claimed without right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such a patentee (or successors) may maintain suit for infringement of that bona fide part; however, he cannot recover costs unless he entered at the Patent Office, before suit, a disclaimer to all parts claimed without right. Unreasonable neglect or delay to enter such disclaimer bars the benefits of this provision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agents to receive models and specimens
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner is authorized to appoint agents in principal cities to receive and forward models, specimens of ingredients, and manufactures intended to be patented or deposited, with transportation chargeable to the patent fund.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appointments are to accommodate different sections of the country; this is a procedural measure to facilitate filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refund to foreign applicants upon rejection for lack of novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: If a foreigner's application is rejected and withdrawn for want of novelty, the Commissioner's certificate is sufficient warrant for the Treasurer to pay back two‑thirds of the duty the applicant paid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory mechanism for partial refund when lack of novelty is determined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affirmation allowed in lieu of oath
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an oath is required, a conscientious scrupulous person may substitute an affirmation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits affirmation instead of oath for those objecting to oaths on conscience grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent fund accounting and reporting duties
rubrics_metrics.description: Moneys paid into the Treasury for patents and for copies shall be credited to a patent fund and appropriated for salaries and expenses of the Patent Office; the Commissioner must annually (January) lay before Congress a detailed statement of expenditures and a list of patents granted and patents becoming public property.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes duty to furnish other information useful to Congress or the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign patent and U.S. application timing (limited rights)
rubrics_metrics.description: A person is not debarred from receiving a U.S. patent merely because it was patented in a foreign country more than six months prior to the U.S. application, provided the invention was not introduced into public and common use in the United States prior to the U.S. application; in such cases the U.S. patent term is limited to fourteen years from the date of publication of the foreign letters‑patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows limited U.S. protection where foreign patent predates U.S. filing but absence of prior U.S. public use is required; statutory term is shortened.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior purchasers/constructors' rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons or corporations who purchased or constructed a newly invented machine/manufacture/composition prior to the inventor's application shall have the right to use and vend the specific thing so made or purchased without liability to the inventor, and such prior purchase/use does not invalidate the patent, except on proof of abandonment or that such purchase/sale/prior use has been for more than two years prior to the inventor's application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects bona fide prior users/buyers; establishes a two‑year cutoff for invalidating patents based on prior public use/purchase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording assignments without charge
rubrics_metrics.description: Assignments, grants, and conveyances of whole or part interests in patents shall be recorded without charge (statutory repeal of prior recording fee).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Removes recording charge for transfers of patent interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal procedure to Chief Justice from Commissioner
rubrics_metrics.description: Where appeals are allowed from the Commissioner's decision, the party may appeal to the Chief Justice of the D.C. district court by notifying the Commissioner, filing written reasons of appeal specifically set forth, and paying $25 into the patent fund.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Chief Justice revises in a summary way confined to the points in the reasons of appeal, hears on evidence produced before the Commissioner at an appointed time, must be furnished originals and grounds of the Commissioner's decision, may examine the Commissioner/examiners under oath, and returns papers with a certificate of proceedings; the certified decision governs further Patent Office proceedings but does not preclude later judicial contest of patent validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioner's power to regulate evidence in contested cases
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner of Patents has the power to make regulations respecting the taking of evidence to be used in contested cases before him.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides administrative rule‑making authority for evidentiary procedure in contested Patent Office proceedings; repeal of prior board of examiners provision is noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of patents – delegated review and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Power to extend patents (previously vested in a board) is vested in the Commissioner; when application for extension is made and 60 days' notice given, the Commissioner shall refer the case to the principal examiner of the class, who will report whether the invention was new and patentable when patented; Commissioner grants or refuses extension on the same principles previously used, and no extension may exceed seven years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes internal examiner review for extension decisions and caps extension duration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees for recording conveyances by word count
rubrics_metrics.description: Fees for recording any assignment, grant, conveyance, power of attorney, or license: $1 for instruments up to 300 words, $2 if over 300 and up to 1,000 words, $3 if over 1,000 words; fees to be paid in advance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets graduated fee schedule for recordation based on length.

rubrics_metrics.name: Franking of Commissioner reports
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner of Patents is authorized to send annual reports of the Patent Office by mail free of postage in the same manner as business mail of the Patent Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural administrative privilege for distribution of reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: False marking and imitation penalties
rubrics_metrics.description: If a person prints, stamps, or affixes 'patent' or like words or imitations on unpatented articles to deceive the public, they are liable to a penalty of not less than $100 plus costs, recoverable in circuit or district courts; one‑half of recovered penalty goes to the patent fund and one‑half to the person who sues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also applies to marking by persons not licensed or not purchased from patentee; statutory enforcement mechanism and distribution of penalties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to mark articles with patent date
rubrics_metrics.description: All patentees and assignees are required to stamp or engrave the date of the patent on each article vended or offered for sale; neglect to do so incurs the same penalty as false marking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Imposes affirmative marking duty on patentees/assignees to indicate patent date; enforcement via penalties described above.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility for shorter term design patents (seven years)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any citizen (or alien residing 1 year and having declared intention to become a citizen) who has produced a new and original design for a manufacture, ornament, print, statue, or configuration not known or used before may apply for a patent; fee is half of the regular sum and the duration of such a patent is seven years, with other applicable regulations applying.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory provision for design‑type protections with reduced fee and 7‑year term; procedural parity with other patent regulations where consistent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oath abroad for applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: The oath required for patent applicants who are not residing in the United States may be taken before any U.S. minister, plenipotentiary, charge d'affaires, consul, commercial agent holding U.S. commission, or before any notary public in the foreign country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows taking required oath outside the U.S. via authorized officials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentability: invention vs discovery (Kemper's Case principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention must be a contrivance or production of something that did not exist before; mere discovery of a property or beneficial effect of something that already existed (i.e., 'discovery' in the sense of finding an existing fact) is not patentable — the applicant must 'invent, contrive, or produce' a new and useful art or improvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge Cranch explains that 'discovery' (bringing to light what existed before) is distinct from 'invention' (creating what did not exist); novelty cannot be satisfied by merely observing that an arrangement has a beneficial effect if that arrangement previously existed and was merely unrecognized for its benefit. Patentability requires novelty of the thing/mode itself, not merely the newfound appreciation of an existing mode's benefit.
